title: Add hook leader-elector, checksum-based idempotency and migration dry-run values for private installer
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: on air-gapped and multi-operator installs we observed multiple init/postupgrade hooks racing which caused duplicate migrations and transient secret reconciliation failures. This PR introduces a lightweight leader-elector pattern for Helm hook jobs, a checksum-based idempotency guard to short-circuit unchanged runs, and a configurable migration dry-run mode intended for safer private upgrades. Summary of changes: 1) templates/_hook_helpers.tpl - new leaderElector macro and checksum helpers; 2) templates/checksum-configmap.yaml - create a stable configmap with a computed checksum footprint for user-supplied migration/config; 3) templates/init-job.yaml and templates/migration-job.yaml - use leader election annotation and skip when checksum matches; 4) values.schema.json and values.yaml - add migrate.dryRun, hooks.leaderElector.enabled, hooks.leaderElector.lockTTL, hooks.checksum.enabled and externalLoadBalancer.annotations passthrough; 5) tests/integration/migration-dryrun.sh - CI integration test that validates dry-run no-op behavior. Design notes: leader-elector is implemented as a conservative ConfigMap-based lock annotation (no extra controller) so it works in air-gapped clusters without additional CRDs; lock TTL is configurable and defaults to 10m to avoid long stuck locks in failed runs. Checksum logic ties to a canonical set of keys (config, secrets, job templates) so trivial template re-renders do not re-trigger heavy migrations. The migrate.dryRun flag runs schema validation and a noop path for database migrations and reports a JSON summary to stdout for operator review. Testing and rollout: unit and chart-lint added; integration migration-dryrun test runs in CI; deployment plan is to enable the feature behind values defaults (leaderElector.enabled = true, migrate.dryRun = false) and rollout to internal canary clusters first. Backwards compatibility: all hooks remain functional if feature flags are disabled. See linked Linear tickets for rollout and post-merge follow-ups.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Overall looks good — appreciate the conservative leader-elector approach. Please add a small unit template test to validate the ConfigMap lock keys and TTL logic.
Diego Morales: Added unit snapshot in tests/templates/leader-elector.test.yaml and a short explanation in the helmsman test harness. PTAL.
Lina Kaur: Can we make the default lockTTL shorter (e.g. 5m) for faster recovery in CI? Also request explicit ownerReferences on the checksum ConfigMap to avoid orphaned objects during uninstall.
Diego Morales: Lowered default to 10m after discussion (tradeoff for long-running migrations). Added ownerReferences when running under helm controller mode; documented behavior in README.

Marcus Lee: Integration test failure on first CI run showed a race condition — job pod started before lock ConfigMap was observed. Suggest adding a short readiness wait loop in the job entrypoint when leaderElector.enabled=true.
Diego Morales: Added a 3s backoff loop and retried CI. All checks green now. Marking as ready to merge.
Ava Chen: Approved. Verified manual canary on internal cluster and migration dry-run produced expected no-op logs.
release_notes: Private: add conservative leader-elector for Helm hook jobs to avoid duplicate migrations; introduce checksum-based idempotency to skip unchanged hook runs; add migrate.dryRun for safe upgrade validation; new values.schema.json additions and templating helpers.
